scope.note: 17 authoritative listed IDs, despite heading saying 16. Only supplement-build.json and supplement-build.md written. No bundled DLL was loaded/executed.

verification.staticVsRuntime: Asset definition/patch expansion proves native codes in source, not live server registration or code execution. Config export is not proof of live application.

pages.title: Building: scaffolding, roofing and carved details
pages.intro: Prepare access and roofing material before finishing the building. Manual Shingle changes acquisition; shingles still need firing. One Roof supplies its own roof blocks, while the shipped Chisel Tools guide handles detailed voxel work.

steps.label: 1. Craft scaffolding
steps.text: Open the native recipe: BBB / SRS / S_S, with planks B, sticks S and rope R. It yields four scaffolds. The exported MaxStability=6 is not proof of a safe six-block unsupported span; do not design around that assumption.

steps.label: 2. Make and fire shingles
steps.text: Manual Shingle adds right-mouse-button shingle/bowl making. The export specifies three-second batches, two shingles per batch and no required table. Its assets do not establish the exact shingle hand setup, so no brick/sneak instruction is supplied here. Raw red shingles fire to burned red at the native 850°C threshold. Raw blue instead fires to black, not blue.

steps.label: 3. Assemble One Roof roofing
steps.text: For red clay use __S / _S_ / S_S: four burned red shingles yield four redclay-standard roof blocks. Separate one-for-one recipes switch standard ↔ dynamic. Use the actual material code, not an invented generic roof-clay. The mod advertises automatic roof building; this export does not explain its placement shortcuts.

steps.label: 4. Obtain stone and shape details
steps.text: Stone Harvesting explicitly supports obtaining full rock blocks with hammer and chisel. Saw Chiseling permits wood chiseling with a saw and supplies sawing animation patches. For repeated details open the shipped Chisel Tools guide: the pantograph copies/pastes and saves shapes; the hand planer removes or adds groups of voxels. Exact harvesting gestures and wear costs remain unverified.

pages.title: Decoration: heraldry, windows and chimes
pages.intro: Planks, cloth, rope and dyes support several decorative products. Make the base item before customizing it at the Heraldry Workbench. Display windows and chimes do not replace dye production or establish room insulation.

steps.label: 1. Build the Heraldry Workbench
steps.text: Gather planks, sticks, resin and plain cloth using the native workbench recipe. Its hammer and chisel are tools with declared durability costs of 20 and 50. Bark Beetle adds an ambient sound to resin-bearing logs and can help locate the resin ingredient.

steps.label: 2. Make a base and apply heraldry
steps.text: Both banner and cape recipes use one plank and two plain cloth pieces. Put the product in the workbench input. Its UI identifies liquid containers holding dye, or water as bleach, and separate Patterns/Shapes tabs. Colors/layers are item attributes, not separate red-cape collectible codes. Follow the native dye-making guide for the liquid supply.

steps.label: 3. Craft a window and arrange the display
steps.text: Four planks in _A_ / A_A / _A_ yield customwindow-plain. Shared Universal Display Library config documents Raise/lower display item (default Left Shift) + mouse wheel, with a 0.25-voxel step. Precise placement is enabled and item overlap disabled in this export. RoomSafeOpening=false does not establish greenhouse/cellar sealing. Window Display Patches also adjusts placement particles for Pewter lamps.

steps.label: 4. Add a chime
steps.text: The wooden wind chime needs rope, one plank and five sticks: _A_ / _B_ / CDC, with two sticks in each C slot and one in D. The copper version uses two bottom slots of two copper rods instead. It is an audio decoration, not a wind meter. Client config controls volume; this export sets main multiplier 3 and maximum distance 16.

pages.title: Workshop: metal tableware and an arrow quiver
pages.intro: Pewter extends casting into tableware, not a new weapon tier. Prepare the alloy and mold before final assembly. Quivers And Sheaths combines leather and a metal buckle into ammunition-storage equipment.

steps.label: 1. Prepare the alloy and mold
steps.text: Pewter requires tin 80–95%, lead 5–10% and copper 1–5%, all within the same alloy batch. A 90/7/3 split satisfies the recipe. Clayform the Tableware Bowl Mold from blue, red or fire clay using its native pattern, then fire it. The shown blue raw/fired molds are actual native codes; clayforming is not an ordinary crafting-grid recipe.

steps.label: 2. Cast tableware, then assemble
steps.text: The bowl mold declares 100 metal units and a four-bowl output. A pewter bowl holds one litre or one meal serving. Bowl + candle makes a candlelamp; matching crock base + lid combine shapelessly into a crock. pagoldsilver adds gold and silver variants in the pewter domain, but static variants do not prove that a running mold accepts those melts: check the native item guidance before committing precious metal.

steps.label: 3. Stitch an arrow quiver
steps.text: Use the basic LNL / LFL / LLL recipe: plain normal leather, an iron buckle, and an arrow marked as a zero-wear pattern tool rather than a declared consumed ingredient. The output is beltbag-back-quiver-arrows in the quiversandsheaths domain, despite mod ID quiversfork. Asset and exported config indicate three ammunition slots. Colored/material variants change attributes, not this collectible code; this is not a claim of extra ordinary backpack slots.

data.chiseltools-guide-text:
Welcome to Chisel Tools
- Hand Planer - scrape away groups of voxels (or add them)
- Hand Wedge Rotate, Mirror, Rotate, and Move voxels on all axis
- Pantograph- Copy and paste between blocks, load and save shapes, merge shapes.
- Ladder Maker- Make any chiseled block climable!
- Path Maker- transform chiseled blocks into decorative path blocks (gives a speed boost when traveling on them). (Note: Requires and uses up path blocks from your inventory in survival mode)
- Paint Brush- replace or add materials (and dyes!) to your chiseled blocks.
- Paint Scraper- remove unused materials from a chiseled block
-Decorative Objects- there are large number of items you can now make chiselable. Most of them you just right click with a chiseled block and they will take on that shape! You'll get the block back if you put another one in, or break the object.

-Commands
-.pf save filename- saves the shape in your held pantograph to disk
-.pf load filename - loads the shape file into your held pantograph
- press "P" (by default) to open the Portfolio (must be looking at a chiseled block). Click on a shape to load it into the held pantograph.
